body: Just chiming in to confirm this happens on MacOS + Mono variants of Godot 4.4 as well. This is a high priority issue for us and we're happy to help fix it. It would be helpful if anyone could point us in a general direction of what could've caused this regression.

@danielkanda Please open a separate bug report with steps to reproduce and if possible a reproduction project. This issue is specific to Android exports on Meta Quest, and while your issue might have a similar symptom (C# export in 4.4 crashing) the cause may be completely different. It _may_ be the same issue but until we've debugged further it's best to treat them separately.

> [@danielkanda](https://github.com/danielkanda) This issue is specific to Android exports on Meta Quest, and while your issue might have a similar symptom (C# export in 4.4 crashing) the cause may be completely different. 

I'm sorry, I wasn't clear. What I meant to say was that this issue is also present in Android exports to Meta Quest built from the MacOS Godot editor. I wanted to add that, as the Godot editor versions @madsbangh listed are all Windows-based.

Just adding some extra context. Not sure if this is relevant, but at launch, I also get the log message:

```

I thought this might be relevant, as the crashing thread is called "GLThread 30"

> I thought this might be relevant, as the crashing thread is called "GLThread 30"

This looks like a mismatch between OpenGL and OpenGL ES versions.

On mobile we use OpenGL ES 3.0, which should be supported. But it refers to 3.3, which is the OpenGL version we target on desktop (and which is roughly a superset of OpenGL ES 3.0).

The code indeed requests 3.3.0,
```
23603e409c0 modules/openxr/extensions/openxr_opengl_extension.cpp          (David Snopek    2022-10-22 20:29:15 -0500 144)      XrVersion desired_version = XR_MAKE_VERSION(3, 3, 0);
23603e409c0 modules/openxr/extensions/openxr_opengl_extension.cpp          (David Snopek    2022-10-22 20:29:15 -0500 145) 
23603e409c0 modules/openxr/extensions/openxr_opengl_extension.cpp          (David Snopek    2022-10-22 20:29:15 -0500 146)      if (!check_graphics_api_support(desired_version)) {
```
but then makes check with:
```
23603e409c0 modules/openxr/extensions/openxr_opengl_extension.cpp          (David Snopek    2022-10-22 20:29:15 -0500  94)      opengl_requirements.type = XR_TYPE_GRAPHICS_REQUIREMENTS_OPENGL_ES_KHR;
```

CC @dsnopek - though this is 2022 code so unlikely to be the cause of this crash, it might just end up being a benign warning.

> > This only seems to happen if the project is using C#
> 
> Could you please confirm by testing without c# build?

Definitely 👍 

Testing on 4.4-stable, I am getting no crashes in my test (32 consecutive app starts), adding a C# solution and dummy script (not sure if the script was necessary), I tested again, and the app crashed on second launch attempt. This made me think it had something to do with C#, and the fact that the crash backtrace has libmonosgen-2.0.so at the top frame. Admittedly I am not familiar with the internals of these things.

I will caveat this with the fact that I sometimes had to launch the app many times (sometimes tens of times) before getting a crash. This makes me unsure about ruling out non-C# projects, and I would definitely take my finding with a grain of salt. I hope it helps anyways.

> Just adding some extra context. Not sure if this is relevant, but at launch, I also get the log message:
> 
> ```
> OpenXR: Requested OpenGL version exceeds the maximum version this runtime has been tested on and is known to support.
> - desired_version  3.3.0
> - minApiVersionSupported  3.0.0
> - maxApiVersionSupported  3.2.0
> ```

This is very unlikely to be related. This is basically the OpenXR runtime saying it supports OpenGL 3.0 through 3.2, but we're using OpenGL 3.3, so something weird might happen. (I think we may have had a similar warning all the way back in Godot 3 with the OpenXR GDNative extension too?)

> On mobile we use OpenGL ES 3.0, which should be supported. But it refers to 3.3, which is the OpenGL version we target on desktop (and which is roughly a superset of OpenGL ES 3.0).

Yeah, actually, we may not actually be using OpenGL 3.3 here, but instead GLES, so maybe the warning is even being incorrectly shown? We might need to have an `#ifdef USE_GLES_OVER_GL` that swaps in the correct version depending on which we're actually using.

In any case, this warning has been around forever, and happens even on non-Mono builds, so I don't think it's related.

> I will caveat this with the fact that I sometimes had to launch the app many times (sometimes tens of times) before getting a crash. This makes me unsure about ruling out non-C# projects, and I would definitely take my finding with a grain of salt.

I've been launching non-C# Godot projects on Quest 2 and 3 through the whole Godot 4.4 dev cycle, frequently 10s of times a day (improving Godot's support for the Meta Quest is my job :-)), and I haven't encountered this specific crash. And looking at the stack trace in the original description, it goes into `libmonosgen-2.0.so`, so this feels very much like it's related to C# in some way
Yeah, I also suspects it's a c# issue. CC @raulsntos

If the issue started with `4.4-dev3`, that seems to indicate it was introduced by https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/88803. That PR changed a bit how we export C# projects to Android, we now use `libmonosgen-2.0.so` directly to host the .NET runtime and load the required .NET Java libraries (`libSystem.Security.Cryptography.Native.Android.jar`).

I've tested this with `4.4-stable` and I've been unable to reproduce. I don't have a Meta Quest, so I'm testing on an Android phone and I get to the alert that says OpenXR failed to start and Godot will start in normal mode, but no crashes.

Do you happen to get any other errors before the crash? Do you see the `JNI_OnLoad: JNI_OnLoad in pal_jni.c` message in the log? It may be useful to export the project with `--verbose`[^1] to get more information, you should then see messages like `.NET: Initializing module...` and `.NET: CoreCLR initialized`[^2].

[^1]: In the export preset, add `--verbose` to **Command Line** > **Extra Args** (needs **Advanced Options** enabled).
[^2]: The message says CoreCLR because we use the CoreCLR API to host the runtime, since Mono shares the same API and we can use it for both. But Android is using the Mono runtime.

@raulsntos Thanks for having a look! I did a test with the --verbose flag on, and I do indeed see the `.NET: CoreCLR initialized` message you mentioned.

I will post the whole log output below for completeness.

Side note: I am sure this is a coincidence, but I was not getting any crashes the first handful of times when testing just now, but when I started `adb logcat`'ing, It crashed on the first attempt right after that. Not sure if there is a timing element here or something, but probably just a coincidence...
